🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Donnie Iris, the Pittsburgh rock legend behind “Ah! Leah!” and “Love Is Like a Rock,” has died at 83.

Iris died on Monday, October 26, 2026, after a three-year battle with bladder cancer, according to multiple reports. Friends and a former bandmate confirmed his passing to CBS and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette.

An Ellwood City, Pennsylvania native known to fans as “King Cool,” Iris found nationwide fame in 1970 as a member of the Jaggerz, earning a gold record for “The Rapper.” He went on to a solo career fronting Donnie Iris and the Cruisers, scoring hits with “Ah! Leah!,” “Love Is Like a Rock,” “My Girl,” “Sweet Merilee” and “Do You Compute?” He also performed with Wild Cherry, of “Play That Funky Music” fame.

With his yellow suit, Buddy Holly-style glasses, distinctive voice and patented scream, Iris stood out from other lead singers — and his songs stayed in rotation on rock radio for decades. He was enshrined as a Pittsburgh Rock 'N' Roll Legend in 2015.

Iris was diagnosed with bladder cancer shortly after his 80th birthday in March 2023. He had surgery, took nearly a year off, and returned to the stage, performing with the Cruisers every couple of months in Pennsylvania and Ohio even after chemotherapy and radiation treatments. In a letter posted October 9 on his Facebook page, he announced his retirement from performing, writing that music had given him “far more than I could ever put into words.” His final performance came September 28 at the grand opening of Citizens Live at The Wylie in Pittsburgh.

“For my money, he was the most beloved Pittsburgh musician of all time,” colleague Joe Grushecky told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. “I don’t know anyone who was loved more than Donnie. He just had that warmth about him, and it came through in his performance.”

Sources: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette; CBS; Nexstar; Beaver County Times; Akron Beacon Journal.
